extractions.quote: Paper ID: 837
The Journal of ECT 35(1):e3-e4, March 2019.
To the Editors: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM) is a rare neurological disorder
We present a case of possible PERM underlying malignant catatonia accompanied by psychiatric symptoms in a woman
Osaka General Medical Center, Osaka, Japan
A 47-year-old woman with normal intelligence
A 47-year-old woman with normal intelligence experienced difficulty with walking, developed incontinence, incoherence, and soliloquy within a month.
At 118 days after discharge from the hospital, no complications related to ECT were observed.

The patient's agitation, incoherence, soliloquy, stated hallucinations, and delusions diminished completely, and her ability to communicate improved dramatically. Moreover, her muscle rigidity reduced, such that she could walk around her room (mRS score, 3).
A therapeutic regimen of oral diazepam and baclofen was initiated
3-day intravenous corticosteroid course (methylprednisolone, 1 g/d) on day 23 of the hospitalization, followed by oral corticosteroid therapy (prednisone, 1 mg/kg per day).

extractions.value: Patient also diagnosed with probable malignant catatonia. Psychiatric symptoms (micromania, Capgras delusions, Cotard delusions, visual and cenesthetic hallucinations) preceded neurological symptoms. mECT dramatically improved both psychiatric and motor symptoms. At follow-up 118 days post-discharge, mRS=1, patient had spastic gait difficulty walking down stairs but could walk without support.
